pages.desc: A business case for connecting Mirchi shows to Gaana, measuring repeat listening and testing whether subscriptions and sponsorship can cover the cost.

sections.title: The decision facing Mirchi Digital
sections.body:
The recommendation in one sentence

Make the app easy and trustworthy first. Then test whether familiar Mirchi voices and Indian music moments give people a reason to listen again. See the steps.

When a listener hears a Mirchi host on FM or sees a clip online, can Mirchi help them find the full show, return next week and eventually pay for more? Start with one city and one recurring show. Mirchi supplies the host, programme and promotion. A Gaana product partner would own changes to its player, plans and billing.

In July–September 2026 ENIL reported ₹33 crore in digital revenue, up 4.6% year on year and equal to 29% of domestic revenue. Digital still recorded an EBITDA loss of ₹7.5 crore, compared with ₹9.8 crore a year earlier. EBITDA measures earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation. Management flagged a possible one- to two-quarter delay to Gaana’s breakeven aim because bringing in customers cost more. ENIL earnings call, November 2026

sections.title: Who needs a better product?
sections.body:
1. The listenerA city commuter knows the host’s voice but may not know the show title. A short link should open the episode the host just mentioned.
  2. The subscriberA listener arriving through earbuds or a trial needs a reason to return after the offer ends. A saved local show can give them one.
  3. The advertiserA local buyer wants to know whether people listened, enquired or visited. Each outcome needs its own count and cost.

ENIL reported 153.1 million monthly active users across its digital properties and around 20 million for Gaana. These have different scopes and potentially overlapping audiences. Dividing one by the other would give a misleading conversion rate. ENIL earnings call, November 2026

sections.title: Why start with returning listeners?
sections.body:
Gaana moved to paid streaming in 2022 while rivals could still introduce people to music for free. In YouGov’s urban India survey, Gaana usage fell from 32% to 22% between 2021 and 2024, while Spotify rose from 24% to 42%. A familiar city host is one reason to choose Mirchi that a competing music catalogue cannot reproduce. See the four-service comparison

Which alternatives were considered?

A cheaper weekly pass may attract buyers who would have bought the monthly plan. Buying installs can increase acquisition cost. A local series can use existing distribution, but still costs money to produce and promote. Test repeat use first, then test a paid offer with listeners who have experienced the show.

sections.title: The proposed listening journey
sections.body:
1. DiscoverHear a short address on FM or tap a tagged link on a social clip.
  2. ListenOpen the exact episode in the app or a lightweight web player. Offer city and language selection only when useful.
  3. ReturnSave the show and resume it. Ask permission for a reminder when the next episode arrives.
  4. Choose a planExplain the price, billing period and renewal before purchase. Offer a relevant series or a longer ad-free session.

The parallel advertiser opportunity is to sell sponsorship for a defined audience with evidence of delivery. Obtain rights and confirm eligible placements before quoting. What M-Ping, Brewery and event sponsorship sell

sections.title: How to run a controlled pilot
sections.body:
Weeks 1–2: the station producer selects a rights-cleared show. The digital team tests links on mobile web and installed apps. Analytics defines an eligible visitor and records playback, return and payment. Weeks 3–6: compare a direct episode landing page with the usual destination, using random assignment within each tagged source. Keep the same creative, programme and offer. Report FM and social separately. Weeks 7–10: follow each group for 30 days. Compare like-for-like listeners before extending the trial.

How much can the team spend?

Illustration: ₹30,000 in production and promotion divided by 300 additional paying listeners is ₹100 per new payer. At ₹25 a month left after variable costs per active payer, that takes four paid months to recover before churn. If many listeners cancel in month two, the campaign can lose money even with strong sign-ups. Explore the payback scenarios

sections.title: When should Mirchi expand?
sections.body:
Primary decision: expand only if the test produces more returning listeners and positive additional contribution over the agreed payback window. Track first plays per eligible arrival, seven-day return per first-time listener, first paid renewal per eligible subscriber and contribution after rights, production, partner fees and promotion. Set the minimum useful lift and sample size with finance and analytics before launch.

Pause if playback failures, refund requests or complaints rise beyond the pre-agreed limits. A positive conversion result with weaker renewal calls for a longer observation window. If the listener trial succeeds, take a separately costed sponsorship package to a city advertiser. Explore an advertiser campaign review

sections.title: Client objectives and campaign delivery
sections.body:
A car, a home appliance, a tin of paint and an insurance policy are bought in different ways. That is why these four companies used Mirchi differently. ENIL, the company that operates Radio Mirchi, described the work in its report for April 2024 to March 2025.

MG Hector took the radio host to the showroom.

Think about buying a car. An ad can help you remember the name, but you will probably want to sit in the car and drive it. Mirchi hosts took part in showroom test drives and talked about the car’s features with participants. For the showroom manager, the next question is simple: how many people who tried the car came back to discuss buying one?

Xiaomi took its products to people’s homes.

Instead of waiting for families to visit an electronics store, its Smart Home League brought demonstrations and challenges to ten residential communities. Residents could see the products in use. Posts about the activity were displayed more than a million times, according to ENIL. That tells Xiaomi how widely the posts appeared. To learn what residents bought afterwards, it would also need sales records.

Dulux made the paint shops the centre of the story.

Dulux sells through dealers: shop owners who stock its paint. It ran a display contest involving 20 selected dealers across five cities. Mirchi hosts visited shops, and entries were featured on radio and online. The people Dulux wanted to involve first were the shop owners themselves. A shop could earn recognition for a good display, and Dulux could give its products a more prominent place in the store.

ACKO met people at a run.

Insurance is usually something people think about when they need a policy. ACKO also appeared in neighbourhood activities and a Neon Run across five cities. The run gave people an enjoyable occasion to encounter the brand. A runner attending, remembering ACKO and later buying a policy are three different outcomes. The report describes the event and leaves the sales outcome open.

These are examples of work delivered. The report gives no fee or profit for each client. ENIL FY25 annual report, pages 15 and 16

One number in plain English. For July to September 2026, ENIL said radio generated 53% of its Indian revenue. Imagine all the money its Indian businesses earned in that quarter as ₹100. About ₹53 came from radio. The figure describes revenue before costs. S2

sections.title: The radio equation
sections.body:
Model

Net Revenue from paid radio ad time = ad seconds available × percentage of ad time sold × actual revenue per second. Use the same city, time of day and time period for every input.

A 5% price reduction needs more than 5% additional sold volume to keep revenue unchanged: 1 ÷ 0.95 − 1 = 5.26%. If capacity or listener ad tolerance is already constrained, the extra volume may not be achievable. Discounting should be evaluated against total profit after direct costs, advertiser retention and future pricing expectations.

Percentage of ad time sold and price are not independent. Prime time, local festivals, premium sponsorships and bundled contracts alter the inventory mix. A national average can hide both healthy cities and weak stations.

sections.title: Proposed pilot: a local advertiser return loop
sections.body:
Analysis

Customer need

A local business needs a credible way to bring relevant people to a store or offer, and an easy way to decide whether to buy another campaign. It may have neither a marketing analyst nor a full agency.

Analysis

Minimum product

Create a scoped campaign brief, a verified landing page or call response mechanism, a delivery log and a concise close-out report. Sell a bounded test before automating the entire sales process.

Analysis

Validation

Select a small, comparable advertiser user group; predefine one primary outcome. Use matched stores or time/geographic comparison groups that do not receive the change when practical. Report uncertainty, not just attributed clicks.

Success criterion to agree before launch: higher extra profit after direct costs from repeat advertisers with acceptable collection days, no rise in delivery exceptions and no deterioration in listener experience.

sections.title: Rights and regulatory dependencies
sections.body:
FM broadcast, online streaming, podcasts, social clips and event music can have different rights and contract conditions. Obtain a rights review for each intended reuse rather than treating a broadcast licence as permission for every platform.

The government’s 2024 expansion announcement sets a 4% annual licence fee for the specified new-city channels. This must not be assumed to replace all existing ENIL licence obligations. S28

The station should establish how renewal exposure and regulatory changes enter deciding where to invest money. Treat potential reforms as scenarios, not approved future savings.

sections.title: Which Mirchi events can someone book or verify?
sections.body:
An active ticket page, a completed sponsor campaign and a concert mentioned by a journalist are different types of evidence. Here is what a buyer or attendee could verify on 23 November 2026.

Listed for sale · Mirchi Neon Run, Chennai

District listed the run at SPR City–Binny for Saturday 28 November 2026 at 6:00 PM, with tickets from ₹299. That shows a public offer to attendees. Ticket price alone cannot give Mirchi’s earnings after discounts, ticketing fees, taxes and production. Dated ticket listing

Delivered · OPPO Mirchi Freshers Season 13

OPPO Reno16 was presenting sponsor and Croma associate sponsor. Students registered for a QR pass, interacted with the phone camera on campus and voted online. ENIL reported 50,000+ registrations, 90,000+ on-ground interactions and 5,000+ Pop Cam activations across a programme spanning 100 colleges and 16 cities. One person can interact several times. The campaign page persists, while the terms give a tentative end date of 30 September 2026. Season terms · ENIL Q2 FY27 presentation

Delivered · music, festivals and city businesses

Royal Stag Boombox 4.0 combined artists and brand zones at the Hyderabad finale on 22 August. Mirchi Tech Onam brought a four-day tech-park activation and cookery contests to Kerala. Vocal for Local recorded more than 40,000 visits. These illustrate what sponsors buy: an audience in a particular place, programming and a measurable activity. The presentation does not disclose the fee or profit for each. ENIL Q2 FY27 presentation

Digital elements that make a physical campaign measurable

Vriksha Bandhan used a live website and photo verification for 983 tree adoptions. Hyundai’s Traffic Quality Index gave commuters a simple traffic score across seven cities. Both show how a campaign can offer ongoing utility or record participation. Attribute only the outcomes that were measured. ENIL Q2 FY27 presentation

Editorial coverage · another organiser may sell the tickets

Mirchi’s music desk also publishes concert calendars. A story about an upcoming concert establishes coverage. Check the named organiser, ticket merchant or sponsor contract before assigning ticket or sponsorship revenue to Mirchi. November concert calendar

Management described roughly 200–250 events a year across 63 markets. In Q2 FY27 it reported ₹20 crore from the business outside traditional airtime sales, with a 30.8% operating margin on that measure. The quarter included festival timing shifts. sections.title: The attendee journey is the retention product
sections.body:
• Discover: relevant city, format, date, artist and accessible information; explain why this event fits the person.
  • Decide: show total price, inclusions, age/access rules, transport information and cancellation terms before checkout.
  • Attend: ticket retrieval, entry throughput, clear help, safe capacity, water and medical support.

sections.title: Proposed event growth system
sections.body:
Start with one repeatable format in two contrasting cities. Give every edition a signed sponsor plan, a downside budget, a cash exposure ceiling and an attendee service plan. Link the promotion source to a first-party or partner-compliant event record so the team can understand conversion without double-counting.

Analysis

Before go / no-go

Secure minimum sponsorship and venue options. Track break-even paid admissions against realistic demand, then set spend-release gates.

Analysis

During execution

Use one operating checklist with named owners. Escalate queues, safety, artist delays and fulfilment gaps quickly. Capture only the data necessary for the intended service.

Analysis

After the edition

Close collections, vendor settlements and sponsor fulfilment. Compare actual profit after direct costs with the quote and track sponsor / attendee return over subsequent editions.

pages.desc: Gaana is an ENIL business. For Radio Mirchi, the relevant question is how listeners find and return to its shows when content travels across services.

sections.title: Why would someone choose Gaana again tomorrow?
sections.body:
THE PRODUCT IDEA · GAANA

A music app cannot rely only on having songs or offering a discount. YouTube Music and Spotify already give many people easy access to music. My idea is to make Gaana feel more personal to everyday life in India using Mirchi's familiar voices, languages, rituals and communities.

This is a proposal to test, not a claim that Gaana has proved these features work. Start by fixing the listening and paywall problems seen in the iPhone audit.

The competition people already know

Find almost any song. Discover popular artists. Listen on familiar devices.

→
A reason Gaana could feel different

“This is my RJ, my language, my commute, my memories and my people.”

Five ideas, each built around a real listening moment

♫01 · YOUR FAMILIAR VOICE

An RJ who understands your day

Imagine: A short Hinglish or regional voice intro before a song during your commute. You can always mute or skip it.

How I would test it

Start with one host and approved voice rights, verified trivia and an optional 10-second introduction. Check whether people return more often than with a normal playlist, after counting voice-generation and rights costs. Location, mood and weather must be optional and appropriately sourced.

☀02 · YOUR DAILY RITUAL

The right music for the moment

Imagine: Morning bhakti, chai-time 90s, Friday Punjabi or songs for a haldi. You choose the moments that matter.

How I would test it

Offer opt-in, time-aware listening in one region first. See whether listeners return for that same moment, with no aggressive notifications or unwanted assumptions about them.

♡03 · YOUR PEOPLE

Listen together, dedicate a song

Imagine: Invite friends to a small “Mehfil” music room on WhatsApp and attach a 15-second spoken dedication.

How I would test it

Start with content cleared for group listening and private, moderated rooms. Count invited people who actually listen and return, not just shares or invites.

★04 · YOUR LOCAL ARTISTS

Be part of a fan community

Imagine: Follow a Punjabi indie artist or a local favourite and hear approved voice messages, new releases or local gig updates.

How I would test it

Build on True Fans Charts with artist consent, one regional fan community and transparent benefits. Look for voluntary repeat use after fulfilment and editorial costs.

↗05 · YOUR MUSIC HISTORY

Bring playlists and memories along

Imagine: Move a permitted playlist from another app and save the song you associate with a trip or wedding.

How I would test it

Playlist imports depend on supported APIs, user permission and music rights. Explain unmatched tracks; keep memories private, exportable and deletable. Measure successful first plays and later return.

When to show a subscription: after someone asks to download music for a commute, remove ads or use an eligible premium group feature—not because a timer has expired. The business must still earn more after music licensing, voice costs, lost ad income and marketing. See the first 90 days, explained step by step.

sections.title: Where does a Mirchi reader go, and who pays?
sections.body:
Product check · 23 November 2026. Mirchi Plus became part of Gaana. ENIL explicitly confirmed the integration in its FY24 annual report. Today a reader can start on Mirchi’s entertainment site and follow a show or subscription link to Gaana. ENIL FY24 annual report · Mirchi Stories

  1. Read on MirchiFind a song chart, interview or photo story. The page carries labelled advertising space.
  2. Choose a showTrending Podcasts links to Gaana. Examples include Sunday Suspense, RJ Kartik Motivation and Mirchi Murga with RJ Naved.
  3. Consider payingThe header offers a ₹1 introductory trial and a Gaana Plus purchase link. Eligibility, renewal price and billing terms depend on checkout.
How much does each activity earn?

ENIL disclosed ₹33 crore of digital revenue in July–September 2026. Its CEO estimated Gaana at about ₹22 crore. That leaves roughly ₹11 crore for the rest of digital. Management names digital solutions as the other large business and also refers to smaller components. Individual shows, ad formats, events and partners have no published revenue split here. Earnings call, pp. 7–8

What does the login journey establish?

The public site shows an editorial-to-streaming handoff and ENIL confirms product integration. The screenshot reports being routed to Gaana during login. The public evidence does not establish a shared identity database, universal single sign-on, migration of every account or transfer of every stream. A returning user’s saved shows, payment entitlement and sign-in state need a consented account test.

Gaana Plus · what could persuade someone to pay?

Subscribers received 72-hour early access to selected Universal Music releases, initially including Badshah and Harrdy Sandhu singles. Better next-song recommendations and controls for mood, activity and genre can make a paid session more useful. ENIL reported record plays per subscriber without publishing the absolute figure. Track second paid renewal and contribution after royalties. ENIL Q2 FY27 presentation

Vivo, Noise and Samsung · three routes to listeners

Vivo preinstallation puts Gaana on a handset before a listener chooses a music app. Noise Buds R1 Gaana Edition bundled one year of Gaana Plus, moving the first renewal decision to the end of the included term. Samsung smart TVs offer a living-room player. ENIL reported over 30 minutes per listening TV user in early usage. None of those figures discloses partner fees or incremental paid renewals. ENIL Q2 FY27 presentation

Artist shows and original audio · what is actually visible?

Gaana DISCVR features emerging artists. ENIL reported over one million views and reach above 438,000. Off The Record distributes artist stories on Instagram and YouTube. Unplugged features artist sessions. Mirchi’s archive also documents original formats such as Varuthi, narrated by Ashutosh Rana, and the Tamil podcast Antharangam Unlimited. These examples show distinct genres and routes to discovery. Direct programme income and current availability for each archived title require separate evidence. ENIL Q2 FY27 presentation · Varuthi launch

Advertiser-funded audio · a buyer can commission a complete series

Girl Effect’s Sunoh used five podcast episodes to address cyberbullying. ENIL reported more than 138,000 listens across the series. A client can commission production and distribution against a defined audience goal. A listen measures consumption. The contract fee, margin and effect on behaviour are separate questions. ENIL Q2 FY27 presentation · M-Ping and Mirchi Brewery

sections.title: What does each platform do for a listener?
sections.body:
Mirchi creates the shows. ENIL integrated Mirchi Plus into Gaana, where readers can find featured podcasts and subscription offers. ENIL operates the businesses. A Mirchi team can commission a series and promote it on air. Placement, entitlement and billing on Gaana require agreement with its product team.

Mirchi Plus on phones, the web and in cars

Launched in India in July 2022 with mobile web, Android and iOS. Launch coverage described short videos, original audio stories and podcasts in English, Hindi, Punjabi, Marathi, Gujarati, Bangla, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam and Kannada. Its help centre lists Android Auto and Apple CarPlay. In the car, the useful task is starting or resuming audio hands-free. Video discovery belongs on a phone. Current device, regional catalogue and sign-in behaviour need an installed-device check. Mirchi Plus help centre · ENIL launch presentation · Launch language list

Three journeys to test

A commuter hears a host mention a series and wants the exact episode. A social viewer taps a clip on mobile web and wants to listen before installing. A bundled Gaana listener wants to understand the next payment before renewing. Record first-play success, time to audible playback, return within seven days and first paid renewal separately. Platform observations

sections.title: How Gaana went from early leader to challenger
sections.body:
1. 2011 · Listening on the webGaana let people choose songs online. Its first month attracted about 1.2 million unique visitors and 11.7 million plays. One person could play many songs.
  2. 2018–20 · Competing for scaleA $115 million funding round backed expansion. Spotify launched in India in 2019. By 2020 Gaana reported 185 million monthly active users.
  3. 2022 · A different price of entryGaana ended free streaming and asked listeners to subscribe. A casual listener could keep using rival free services without making that decision. Mirchi separately launched Mirchi Plus for original shows.
  4. 2023–26 · Rebuilding paid listeningENIL acquired the Gaana undertaking in December 2023. By the September 2026 quarter, management was discussing the cost of attracting paying users and the timing of breakeven.

Read the contemporary evidence. Early web usage · Funding and reported reach · 2022 paid pivot · ENIL FY25 annual report · ENIL earnings call, November 2026

Spotify moved ahead of Gaana in this survey. Respondents could use several services. The survey cannot tell us whether a particular listener switched apps or why. YouTube here is the survey’s YouTube category. YouGov India Media Morph, 2024

What made Spotify easier to choose?

Free listening reduced the risk of trying it. Spotify also invested in local discovery. It reported that international music accounted for nearly 70% of listening at launch in India, while local music exceeded 70% five years later. A listener who found familiar music, built playlists and kept returning had a reason to stay. The paywall change and local discovery are plausible explanations. Neither explains a measured fraction of Gaana’s decline. Spotify India at five years

What does the 300 million headline tell us?

Spotify reached 300 million paying subscribers worldwide in Q2 2026 and 306 million in Q3. It reported 788 million monthly active users worldwide in Q3. India’s paid subscriber count cannot be derived from those totals. Spotify Q3 release

What alternatives does a listener see today?

The November India comparison lists JioSaavn at ₹99/month, Spotify at ₹139 and YouTube Music at ₹119. Student offers lower the entry price. JioSaavn competes on Indian music and language discovery. YouTube competes on video discovery and familiar creators. Pocket FM competes for the next episode with timed or coin-based unlocks. Kuku FM competes with serial stories and premium access. Open Gaana’s price section below for the different offers visible across purchase paths. India price comparison checked 17 November 2026 · Pocket FM unlocks

Where can Mirchi compete on its own terms?

Test a city host’s daily picks, a local-language serial and an easy return to the last episode. A national music catalogue alone gives a Spotify user little reason to change habits. Compare seven-day return and four-week listening with ordinary playlist traffic. A successful first play alone cannot justify the production cost.

sections.title: What can an advertiser buy from Mirchi?
sections.body:
A brand can pay for access to an audience, for a creative team to make something, or for an event that people attend. A contract may combine all three. Count its revenue once.

M-Ping · buy targeted advertising

A local retailer can specify the audience and pay to deliver a recorded message across participating publishers. Software selects eligible placements. Ads may run before or during audio. A companion banner gives a listener something to tap where supported. Confirm targeting, publisher access and dynamic insertion in the current order. Measure completed listens, cost per thousand impressions and the cost of a qualified response. M-Ping · Mirchi launch announcement

Mirchi Brewery · commission a campaign

The creative team develops the idea and produces the work. Gradeup used Brewery for a series of brand films. A buyer might commission a host-led reel, a branded audio drama or a podcast segment. Price production, talent and distribution separately. Check completion, qualified enquiries and the money left after production costs. ENIL FY25 annual report · Gradeup campaign

Gaana Ad Network · confirm what can actually be bought

The supplied brief lists audio spots, sponsored playlists, homepage takeovers and mobile banners. Gaana moved to a subscription-led model in 2022. A historic format list cannot establish the size of a current free tier. Before quoting a client, request a dated rate card, eligible listener count, placement rights and delivery forecast. Protect the ad-free promise for paying listeners.

Live events with digital coverage · connect attendance to follow-up

For a run or concert, a sponsor may buy naming rights, a branded registration page, event coverage or a social challenge. Someone might see a clip, register and attend. Count those stages separately. In the ACKO example, Mirchi combined neighbourhood activity with a Neon Run. Compare sponsor revenue and ticket income with venue, staffing and production costs. ENIL FY25 annual report

Connect an advertiser’s city objective with a credible host, useful local content and a relevant experience. Make delivery and response visible.

sections.title: What should be difficult to copy?
sections.body:
YouTube Music benefits from YouTube's creator/remix and video ecosystem and some bundles; Spotify has broad discovery and continuity. Exact India catalogue, plan and feature comparisons must be checked by market and date. Gaana cannot assume catalogue or pricing parity. A generic AI DJ is easy for competitors to build. A permissioned network of recognisable Mirchi RJs, regional editorial judgment, local rituals and social dedications could create cultural intimacy: it becomes a defensible advantage only if users return more often and the full cost of that relationship is sustainable.

Falsification test: randomise eligible listeners between a rights-cleared RJ ritual and a comparable non-RJ curated experience. sections.title: People came to play music. The app keeps selling to them.
sections.body:
GAANA IPHONE APP · WHAT WAS OBSERVED

The supplied iPhone screenshots show a music player covering important buttons, paid offers competing with playlists, and pricing that is difficult to interpret. A repeating subscription popup was also reported. The first job is to make listening and buying understandable.

Visible in supplied screenshotsCovered buttons, multiple offers, conflicting messages
Reported by the userRecurring popup with delayed Close button
Still needs testingHow often it happens and how many customers it affects

What I would fix, in order

P0 means fix the essentials first, P1 means improve the experience next, and P2 means polish the details. These labels describe priority, not proven revenue impact.

P0 · FIX FIRST · LISTENING CONTROL

Stop forcing people back into the subscription screen

The issue: the tester reports a full-screen offer returning every 1–2 minutes, with Close temporarily locked.

The fix: let Close work immediately, remember dismissal and offer paid plans only when someone requests a benefit.

How I would confirm the change

Reproduce across iOS account states, then count interrupted sessions, offer dismissals, successful first plays, complaints and later return. Churn or App Store review impact is not proven by the screenshots.

P0 · FIX FIRST · USABLE BUTTONS

Uncover songs and payment actions

The issue: the bottom music player and floating tabs overlap Monthly Plan, the Noise bundle’s “SHOW ME” button and Trending Songs.

The fix: keep the page content clear of both fixed bars, including the iPhone’s safe-area space.

How I would confirm the change

Test on several iPhone sizes, text enlargement, VoiceOver and while scrolling. Make sure every important button is visible, reachable and tappable.

P0 · FIX FIRST · PAYMENT TRUST

Tell people what they pay and receive

The issue: “Pay for 12 Months, Get 1 Month Free” and “First Month is FREE” appear with a ₹709 upfront price. The displayed monthly equivalent also does not match simple 12-month division.

The fix: show amount due today, months of access, next charge and cancellation terms in the same way on every screen.

How I would confirm the change

Compare the real iOS payment sheet, receipts, web offers and available plans. ₹709 ÷ 12 = ₹59.08 and ₹709 ÷ 13 = ₹54.54; the observed ₹58.27/month label needs reconciliation. Do not present a charge-upfront offer as a zero-charge trial without the real terms.

Then make the paid offer easier to understand

P1 · IMPROVE NEXT · HOME

Stop letting promotions crowd out music

A cyan banner and “Time’s Ticking” offer compete for the first scroll. Make the play/resume action prominent and use one clear, dismissible paid offer instead of multiple competing messages.

P1 · IMPROVE NEXT · PRICING

Explain ₹709, ₹799 and ₹899

₹799 is shown as a crossed-out comparison, not a verified third iOS plan. Distinguish an annual recurring offer from a one-time annual purchase and disclose any Noise hardware renewal terms.

P2 · POLISH · WORDING

Write like a trusted music brand

Replace phrases such as “First Month FREE !!” and “No More Ads Your Way” with clear benefits. Show “Save ₹90” only if ₹799 is a verified like-for-like reference price.

Full quality-assurance checklist and research limits

The screenshots cannot show the actual purchase receipt, 1-star review effect or how many customers leave. Re-check trial eligibility, iOS/web prices, cancellation and restoration, failed payment, offline listening, bundle redemption, player and keyboard overlap, content rights, login persistence, notification prompts, playlist imports, accessibility labels and support handling.

Priority here means urgency to validate and repair, not estimated revenue impact. A fix is successful only when it works on devices and listening, trust and commercial measures are stable or better.

Where next?Check the pricing arithmeticWhat to fix firstSee the 90-day plan

sections.title: How to judge the money and time saved

• For staff tools, count the complete task. Include checking and correcting AI output. Saving drafting time helps only when total time per approved result falls.

  • For a new paid AI product, test whether customers pay and return. Include model usage, audio processing, storage, editing, support and sales costs.

Illustrative calculation. If 20 editors each save 30 minutes a day over 22 working days, that is 220 hours per month. At an assumed ₹500 per hour, the capacity value is ₹1.10 lakh. sections.title: Don't build five features while the basics are broken
sections.body:
WHAT SHOULD WE FIX FIRST?

The supplied Gaana screens raise two immediate problems: parts of the app are hard to tap, and the paid offers are hard to understand. A repeated popup was also reported. Fix those basics before trying to make Gaana more personal.

FIRST · APP REPAIRS

Help people listen without hassle

Stop recurring subscription interruptions, prevent the music player from hiding buttons and show the actual amount and duration of each plan.

Why first? A beautiful new feature won't help if users cannot enjoy a song or trust a payment.

SECOND · SMALL USER TEST

Give people a reason to return

Invite a small group to try an optional Mirchi voice intro or a morning/commute playlist. Compare their voluntary return with listeners using the regular experience.

Why second? Returning by choice is more valuable than opening the app after another push notification.

THIRD · ONLY IF IT HELPS

Try music shared with friends

Test a private Mehfil song room or dedication once music rights and safety are approved. Leave fan clubs and playlist import for later validation.

Why third? Sharing is useful only if friends actually listen and the experience is safe and sustainable.

How would this happen?See the visual 90-day planSee what was observedExplore the five ideas

Who decides? Gaana owns its app and subscription changes; Radio Mirchi contributes hosts, content and regional expertise. These are proposed experiments, not approved releases. Revenue, app quality, user safety and rights must be checked before expansion.

sections.title: Measure local advertiser renewals
sections.body:
Offer a limited catalogue by objective, city and budget, supported by a clear delivery plan and response measurement. Start with a category that repeats frequently enough to evaluate within a practical window. A sales-assisted workflow is a reasonable first version; self-service comes after the offer is repeatable.

  • Primary: extra 90-day advertiser profit after direct costs and repeat booking.
  • Checks that protect service and profit: collection days, deal discount, delivery exceptions, sales time and listener experience.
  • Evidence: matched accounts or a phased rollout; track displaced radio or solution spend.
  • Stop: higher gross billings with lower retained margin or longer credit exposure.

sections.title: Evaluate repeat events
sections.body:
Put event discovery, booking partners, sponsor fulfilment and the event budget into one operating view. Preserve attendee consent and ticket-platform contractual boundaries. The product should support a faster, better proceed or stop decision, not merely make another listing page.

  • Primary: actual edition profit after direct costs and cash conversion.
  • Customer: entry wait, issue resolution, sponsor fulfilment and subsequent return.
  • Scale: comparable editions meet economics and service gates across cities.
  • Stop: the model depends on uncontracted sponsorship, unrealistic attendance or unsustainable local workload.

sections.title: Improve content discovery and production
sections.body:
For content continuity, start with one franchise and preserve the destination from social post to story page to app. For AI, observe a real workflow first: transcription, clip selection, tagging, local adaptation or campaign report assembly may be candidates. Compare turnaround and error rate against the current process.

Quality and rights are part of the product

Keep editorial review, talent permission, licensed-use boundaries and factual checks in the release criteria. A faster output is valuable only if it is usable and creates no extra correction or rights burden.

sections.title: From a frustrating first visit to a listening habit
sections.body:
THE PRIORITY · GAANA MUSIC APP

The supplied Gaana iPhone screens show paid-plan buttons being covered by the music player, crowded subscription promotions and confusing prices. A frequently reopening subscription popup was also reported. Those are reasons to investigate and fix the experience before spending effort on new AI features.

Seen in the screenshotsCovered buttons and confusing offers
Reported by the testerRepeated subscription popup
Not yet establishedHow many users leave or stop paying

What happens over the 90 days?

The dates below are an example sequence, not promises. The next stage starts only if the previous work is safe, usable and supported by evidence.

  1. 01Days 1–15Understand the problem

    See exactly where people struggle

    Watch new and returning listeners try to play music, close offers and choose a plan. Check the actual prices shown at payment.

    ExampleDoes the ₹709 plan charge immediately? Why is the monthly figure different when we divide it by 12?

    Before moving on: we can reproduce the problems, show screenshots of each issue and explain the real payment terms.

  2. 02Days 16–30Fix the basics

    Let the listener stay in control

    Stop subscription offers appearing again and again, make Close work immediately, move the music player away from purchase buttons and make plan differences readable.

    ExampleWhen someone taps a monthly plan, they can read its price and tap Subscribe without the floating player blocking it.

    Before moving on: key buttons work, payment information agrees across screens and people can start listening without unwanted interruption.

  3. 03Days 31–60Test a reason to return

    Bring a familiar Mirchi voice into Gaana

    With permission, try one optional regional-language RJ voice introduction and a useful daily moment, such as the morning commute or chai-time 90s songs. Keep it easy to skip or turn off.

    Example“Your drive home: here's a song from the 90s,” spoken briefly by a familiar, rights-cleared host voice.

    Before moving on: people choose to return more often than listeners without this feature, without making the experience expensive or annoying.

  4. 04Days 61–90Decide what deserves investment

    Test sharing, then make a decision

    Try a small, private group listening room with song dedications, only if playback rights and safety checks allow it. Compare whether people actually listen together and return.

    ExampleShare a song room through WhatsApp, add a short voice dedication and see whether invited friends listen—not just click.

    At day 90: recommend continuing, improving or stopping each idea based on listener experience and the real cost of running it.

HOW WOULD WE KNOW IT WORKED?

Three questions, not a wall of dashboards

▶

Can people play music?

More people start the song they came for, with fewer interruptions and blocked taps.

↻

Do they choose to return?

Count listeners who come back and play music on another day, not just app opens.

₹

Does it make business sense?

Money earned after the extra costs of music rights, voice technology and promotion.

No improvement is assumed. Compare results with a similar group that did not receive the new feature. A paid subscription renewed a year later cannot be proven inside a 90-day test.

A SEPARATE BUSINESS PROBLEM

Not every improvement belongs to Gaana. Mirchi also needs better ways to help local advertisers get value from campaigns and decide which events are worth repeating. This is a separate workstream, not four more things for one Gaana team to build.

01

First month: understand a station

Talk to listeners, producers and advertisers in one city. Find the most important repeated problem.

02

Second month: fix one issue

Try one improvement, such as easier campaign reporting or finding a popular show online.

03

Did advertisers book again? Did the change save time or make more money after its costs?

Show the detailed station delivery checklist

Days 1–15: confirm ownership and measurement. Days 16–30: agree the problem, cost and an honest comparison. Days 31–60: release one focused improvement with tracking. Days 61–90: review customer results, cash collected and direct costs, then decide whether to repeat it in another city.

One city and one accountable owner come before expansion. Read the business recommendations.

sections.title: Did the change make listening better?
sections.body:
HOW TO TELL IF IT ACTUALLY HELPED

It is easy to count app downloads or subscription clicks. The more useful question is whether people can listen, choose to come back and find enough value to pay—without making the business less profitable.

THREE MEASURES I WOULD SHOW A BUSINESS HEAD
▶

First successful play

Out of people trying to listen, how many actually hear the song or show?

↻

Repeat listening

How many willingly listen on more than one day in a week? This would be my main proposed habit measure.

₹

Money left after costs

Subscription and ad income minus the extra costs of music, AI voice, promotions and support.

Always watch for hidden harm: crashes, users leaving, unwanted popups, refunds, complaints and lost ad income. No uplift or customer numbers are assumed.

How I'd check the popup fix

BEFORE THE CHANGE

Record how often users see or dismiss the popup, whether they can start music, and whether they return a week later.

AFTER THE CHANGE

Allow immediate close, stop repeated timer-based interruptions and show subscription offers when someone needs a premium feature.

Compare fairly: where ethical, use comparable groups and the same price/eligibility. If the old experience is harmful, fix it for everyone and be clear that a before/after comparison cannot fully prove causation.

For product interviewers: detailed measures and test design

Acquisition: qualified arrivals by radio, organic, paid and partner channels. Activation: successful intentional first play and time to music. Habit: weekly listeners with a meaningful audio session on two or more distinct days. Monetization: eligible purchase starts, completed payments, contribution after CAC, royalties, app fees, AI inference and displaced ads. Retention: meaningful listening at D1, D7 and D30, then actual paid renewal later. Define a meaningful play duration with analytics before reporting.

Experiment: use stable user-level assignment for eligible iOS non-subscribers where appropriate; distinguish app version, acquisition source and plan eligibility. Primary: first intentional play and D7 return per eligible listener. Secondary: incremental profit after direct costs. Safety checks: errors, exits, support, unwanted notifications, refunds and ad loss. Set duration and sample size only after observing actual baseline data.

Plain English: D7 means a user returns seven days after joining; CAC means money spent to acquire a customer; a control group is a comparable group that did not receive the new feature. These are measures to establish, not numbers that the screenshots reveal.

A proposed shared lens is extra profit after direct costs from repeat customer relationships. It needs a business-specific definition; a sponsor, an advertiser and a subscriber cannot share one base number.

sections.title: Definitions that need to be explicit
sections.body:
• Activation: a successful value moment, not an install or a login. Define the required listening or campaign outcome before measurement.
  • Retention: the fraction of a starting user group that meets the defined value event in a later window. Keep trial, partner and paid user groups separate.
  • Profit after direct costs: net recorded revenue minus the costs included in the agreed cost breakdown. State which variable, direct and allocated costs are included.
  • Extra results caused by the change: the change versus a credible estimate of what would have happened without the change, not the number of people with a campaign tag.
  • Repeat event customer: one person attending a second relevant edition, counted once using information they have permitted us to link.
  • Actual price earned: actual revenue after discounts and the adjustments agreed with finance.

sections.title: The important rates, with simple formulas
sections.body:
MeasureHow to calculate itWhat to keep consistent
First-play conversionPeople with a successful first play ÷ eligible people who entered the journey × 100.Use people, not a mixture of visits, installs and accounts. Define a successful play.
7-day / 30-day returnPeople from the starting group who listen in the chosen later window ÷ people in that starting group × 100.State whether you mean exactly day 7, any day in week 2, or a rolling window.
Episode completionEligible episode starts that reach the agreed completion point ÷ eligible starts × 100.State the completion threshold; report episode length and repeated starts separately.
Paid renewalSubscriptions that renew successfully ÷ subscriptions due to renew in the period × 100.Separate annual, monthly, trial and partner plans. A cancelled future renewal is not always immediate loss of access.
Revenue per paying userSubscription revenue for a period ÷ the agreed average number of paying users in that period.State monthly or annual, exclude or include taxes consistently, and separate paying from active users.
Customer acquisition costIncluded marketing, partner and incentive spend ÷ new paying customers from that spend.A device shipped or a free trial started is not a paying customer.
Radio ad-time soldAd seconds sold ÷ ad seconds available for sale × 100.Compare the same city, station, time of day and period.
Radio price earnedRecorded ad revenue after agreed adjustments ÷ ad seconds sold.Use the same treatment of agency fees, discounts and bundles.
Advertiser repeat rateAdvertisers who buy again in the chosen window ÷ advertisers eligible to buy again × 100.Also measure repeat spend and profit: one small repeat order can hide lost budget.
Booking conversionCompleted paid bookings ÷ eligible booking journeys started × 100.Track people, orders and tickets separately; a couple ticket is not one attendee.
Paid attendancePaid-ticket holders who enter ÷ valid paid-ticket holders expected × 100.Separate complimentary passes, refunds, no-shows and capacity.
Sponsor renewalEligible sponsors who book the next comparable edition ÷ eligible sponsors × 100.Also compare retained sponsorship value, cash collected and delivery costs.
Event direct profitSponsor income + ticket income after deductions + other contracted income − included event delivery costs.List the included costs. Direct profit is not the same as final company profit.
AI usable-output rateAI outputs accepted after the agreed review ÷ outputs reviewed × 100.Include review time, correction time, rights checks and serious errors when judging value.

sections.title: Three experiments worth designing properly
sections.body:
ExperimentPrimary testDesign caution
Partner activation journeyExtra profit from users who keep returning per eligible user group.Randomise or phase within comparable partner user groups; preserve offer and season.
Advertiser package90-day repeat profit after direct costs versus current offer.Account for sales selection, account size and spending shifted from an existing offer.
Event reminder / return loopExtra net ticket profit after direct costs from permitted audience.Use a comparison group that does not receive the change; include discount cost, refunds and substitution between events.

Choose sample size from the actual starting result, the smallest improvement worth detecting, allocation and desired statistical precision. No sample-size number is invented here. Predefine the decision window and checks that protect service and profit, and avoid repeatedly stopping the test at the first positive result.

sections.title: How to measure results across offline and online
sections.body:
On-air codes, tagged links, unique landing pages, booking references and matching customer records can identify observed response. They do not automatically capture all radio exposure or establish causation. Pair response tracking with comparison groups that do not receive the change or matched comparisons where feasible, and report uncertainty.

The stakeholder-friendly dashboard

Show what was delivered, what people did, what changed versus the comparison and how much profit after direct costs remained. Keep these four layers separate so a reach metric does not quietly become a revenue claim.

sections.title: Assumptions & definitions
sections.body:
Assumptions & definitions

All models are hypothetical scenarios, not Gaana or ENIL operating disclosures. Default inputs and presets do not report actual CAC, churn, paid users, margins, ticket costs, radio yield or product impact. The observed ₹709/year public offer is not the same as the illustrative ₹600 of net recorded subscription service revenue in the first model.

Gaana subscriptions

Starts with already-paying users: annual unit contribution = net recorded annual service revenue × (1 − variable cost share) − annual direct service cost. Year-one cohort contribution = users × (annual unit contribution − acquisition cost). Renewals are a separate next-year illustration using the same unit margin and the assumed renewal rate. Paid renewal does not affect the upfront Year-one contribution. CAC recovery months spread annual unit contribution evenly as an illustrative comparison, not the cash collection schedule, customer lifetime value or statutory accounting. Recognised revenue must be net of applicable tax, refunds, store / partner shares and revenue recognition rules.

FM radio yield

Revenue = available ad seconds × sold percentage × net realised ₹ per sold second. The alternative discounts net price while varying sold seconds. The model does not subtract any incremental sales/production expenses, model differences by station/daypart, or imply that more ad loading is listener-safe. Profit needs a separate cost bridge.

Live events

Event revenue = paid attendees × net organiser receipt per ticket + contracted sponsorship + net ancillary income. Direct cost = fixed direct spend + attendees × variable cost. Ticket receipt is after platform fees and relevant taxes; GST, allocations and corporate overhead must be handled consistently and not subtracted twice. Sponsor income must be contracted and collectible; exclude speculative projections. Break-even attendees are the ceiling of uncovered fixed costs divided by net ticket contribution (when positive), capped by available ticket capacity. Attendance is paid admissions only, not gross footfall.

Decision integrity: validate all baseline numbers, cohort definitions, cash timing, GST, corporate overhead and net organiser receipt with finance before committing spend. Prefer controlled incrementality over a favorable illustrative outcome.

sections.body:
Research date: 21 November 2026, India time. Financial cut-off: latest available Q2 / H1 FY27 disclosures. Source hierarchy: filed financial tables for scoped figures; management disclosures for strategy; official product pages for current propositions; public observations for experience; independent industry research for market context.

LabelMeaningLimit
ReportedCompany / official source says it.Not independently audited unless explicitly stated.
ObservedA public browser surface was inspected in this session.Session, region, viewport and eligibility may affect behaviour.
Listing evidenceStore description, release notes, ratings or screenshots.Does not establish installed-app behaviour.
Hypothesis / proposedOriginal analysis or a potential test.Not a confirmed defect or promised business result.

Public browsing used a signed-out in-app browser. Desktop default was 1280 × 720. Mobile responsive checks used a 390 × 844 viewport; these are browser emulation, not a physical handset or native app test. pages.title: Test the listener and advertiser decisions
pages.desc: Explore whether acquiring a paying listener can cover its cost, then assess what an advertiser received and whether a renewal makes sense.

sections.title: How long does it take to recover the cost of a new subscriber?
sections.body:
Suppose a city show costs ₹30,000 to promote. Each active paying listener contributes ₹25 per month after variable costs. Choose a result to see how customer acquisition changes the decision. These are illustrative inputs.

150 extra payers

₹30,000 ÷ 150 = ₹200 per payer. Recovering this takes eight paid months. If the typical payer leaves after four months, the campaign falls short by ₹100 per payer.

300 extra payers

₹100 per payer takes four paid months to recover. A listener who leaves after two paid months contributes ₹50. Check the actual renewal distribution before expanding.

600 extra payers

₹50 per payer takes two paid months. Check that the additional payers were caused by the campaign and that discounts did not reduce the ₹25 monthly contribution.

sections.body: Objective: encourage weekend test drives. The example booking covers 30 radio ads and one host appearance. The station log confirms 28 ads and the appearance. Two ads remain due. Agree replacement slots with the dealer.

sections.title: What the dealer can measure
sections.body: The dealer recorded 18 test drives during the campaign weekend. Eight participants used the campaign booking code. Code use shows a recorded response. A comparable weekend or a controlled test would help estimate additional visits caused by the campaign.

sections.title: Listener product decision
sections.body:
Proposed pilot for one local show. Choose the observed result to see the next product decision. These are hypothetical outcomes.

People open the host’s link but rarely start listening

Check that the link opens the promised episode, the play control works on mobile web and the audio is available in that region. Compare successful plays per eligible visit before buying more traffic.

People listen once but seldom return

Test a visible next episode or a voluntary show reminder. Compare seven-day return among first-time listeners with the current experience, and monitor opt-outs.

Listeners return and a sponsor wants more ad time

Test one placement. Compare net sponsor income per eligible listener, completion and repeat listening against the current ad load. Expand only if the extra income covers production and the loss of future listening.
